question: On real merged pull requests, does the lead solve the problem as often when its whole-file reads are handed to a subagent? Pass or fail by each pull request's own tests, with cost and wall time beside it.
rule: The six tasks of mlflow-b2-fair-turns (eleven real merged MLflow pull requests, each a nine-prompt session graded by the pull request's own tests) with the largest merged change by lines: PR26267 (274), PR26307 (207), PR26270 (165), PR26269 (140), PR26300 (108), PR26311 (106). Chosen 2026-11-15 by size alone, after a free replay of archived unmodified sessions showed the trigger fires on this set (7 of 7 sessions) and never on the PostHog nine-turn tasks (0 of 6; their reads are ranged). The reading prompts are scripted, so the firing is prompted; the problem and the grading are real. A delegate session in which the hook never fired is named and enters no figure. Canary first: one delegate session of PR26311, kept as rep 0 if the design is unchanged after it.
